###chapter 1
"Hey, boss?" Lysander cleared his throat, sounding like he was stepping on eggshells. "Thane sent another one. The divorce papers. Again."

He looked like he wanted to swallow his tongue. "He, uh... he said if you let Briar take the co-Managing Director spot, he might actually reconsider. He’s already bragging to the pack, though. Saying you're too obsessed with him to ever go through with it, and—"

Lysander choked on his next breath. 

Elara sat straight up in her hospital bed. Her hands didn't shake. She grabbed a pen and scribbled her name right on the dotted line. No drama. Just the scratch of ink on paper.

Three months. She’d been stuck in this white box of a room for three damn months, breathing in bleach and listening to the hum of medical monitors. And this? This was the seventh time he’d shoved these papers in her face.

The first time was right before his trip to the Grimroot Consortium. He had some weird medical issue, but his ultimatum was simple: hand over sole control of the pack accounts, or sign the papers.

The second time? Their seventh anniversary. He wanted Briar—her old nanny's kid—to move back into the main house. Just like the old days, he said.

Number three came on her birthday. He wanted Briar to nanny their son, Asher. "So you can focus on work, Elara." Right.

Number four was on his own birthday. He needed Briar as his personal assistant.

Number five happened after Briar dragged Elara's name through the mud in front of the whole pack. Thane’s peace offering? "Let it go, or sign the papers."

Number six landed on Asher’s sixth birthday. He wanted Briar to move into the Managing Director’s suite. "Since you're never in there anyway."

Every single time, Elara had ripped those papers to shreds right in front of the messenger. She’d kept her face blank, even while her chest felt like it was cracking open.

Then she almost died. She took a hit from a chemical weapon to save the pack, destroying her own body. She thought maybe she’d get a thank you. Or some pity.

Instead? She got round seven. But this time, there was a catch: make Briar co-Managing Director. 

That was it. The absolute limit. A total slap in the face.

She finally got it. The marriage had been dead in the water for years. 

Six chances. All wasted. There was nothing left to save. She was taking Asher and getting the hell out.

"Boss..." Lysander stared at the signed page, his jaw practically hitting the floor. "You... you actually signed it? Why now?"

Elara looked up, a tiny, tired smile on her lips. "My mom always said seven is the magic number. If you can't fix something in six tries, the seventh isn't going to save it."

The world wasn't the same anymore. Werewolves didn't hide in the woods. They lived right alongside humans, running multi-million dollar companies in the city. 

With cameras everywhere, shifting in public was a death sentence, so the pack structure still mattered. 

But the old ways were fading. The new moon festivals only happened inside pack territory now. Everyone showed up, unless you married a human. 

Almost everyone worked in the city. Only the omegas, Lunas, and betas stayed behind to guard the land and keep the lights on.

Thane was the second-richest guy in New York. But honestly? Elara built that empire. Her plans, her deals, her secret tricks—she made them second only to the Grimroot pack.

And what did she get? Cold shoulders. He treated her like garbage to punish her for some old mistake that wasn't even her fault.

She was done begging for a scrap of his attention. Done waiting for him to care.

From now on, it was just her and Asher. Honestly, their kid was the only reason they’d gotten hitched in the first place.

Elara slid the paper over, then swung her legs out of the bed.

Lysander gasped, eyes wide. "Wait—you can walk?!"

The chemicals had paralyzed her. The doctors said she’d never stand again.

Every step felt like hot glass slicing through her nerves, but she didn't flinch. After two months of staring at the ceiling, pain meant she was alive.

She smirked, keeping her mouth shut. Two months in bed and one month of secret rehab gave her plenty of time to think. 

A broken marriage is like a cracked egg. You can't glue it back together.

Nobody cared enough to check on her, so they didn't know she’d cured herself using her own medical tricks.

"Tell Thane," she said, her voice dead calm, "he doesn't need a co-Managing Director. Once the divorce goes through, he can just give Briar the whole job."

Lysander didn't argue. Honestly, he was relieved she was finally walking away from people who didn't deserve her.

Elara was the smartest, toughest Managing Director the pack had ever seen. Too bad her own husband was too blind to notice. The whole marriage was a mistake from day one.

Years ago, wolves watched humans choose their own partners and got jealous. They begged the Eternal Spirit to break the mate bond.

They got their wish. But they also got cheating, lies, and broken hearts.

Guys like Thane didn't understand how human love worked—the freedom to choose one person and stick with them. He just hated being stuck with Elara. If they hadn't had that one wild night, he never would've put a ring on her finger.

As Elara reached the exit, bass boomed through the walls. Loud, happy, mocking music.

"What's the noise?" she asked.

Lysander looked down, embarrassed. "The coronation. Thane is announcing Briar as the new co-Managing Director tonight. He invited alphas from other packs, but told them to leave their Lunas at home. He figured you wouldn't show up to stop him."

Elara smiled, but her eyes were dead. Of course he did. The other Lunas would've called him out on his BS.

She snatched the signed divorce papers back from Lysander and walked out of the hospital, still wearing her thin, paper-thin hospital gown.

Lysander tried to grab her arm, but she was already down the hall.

The music got louder. Pack members she’d literally bled for stared at her, mouths open in shock.

She pushed open the doors to the grand hall, and the entire room went dead silent.

"Is that Elara?"

"She's alive?"

"Wait, she's walking? No wheelchair?"

Thane—tall, gorgeous, and totally in control—froze right in the middle of his speech.

"Elara?" His voice was smooth, but his eyes were ice. "What are you doing here? You should be in bed."

Classic Thane. Playing the caring husband for the crowd while his eyes warned her to back off. He’d never looked at her the way he looked at Briar.

"Is that really her?" a guest whispered. "She looks... awful."

Her hair was a messy nest. Her skin was pale and sickly. The cheap hospital gown hung off her thin frame, looking ridiculous next to all the designer suits and diamonds.

Elara didn't give a damn.

Before Thane could even move, she marched right up to him and slammed the papers against his chest.

"Don't bother making her co-Managing Director," she said, her voice echoing in the silence. "Just give her the whole title. I signed the papers. We're done."

The words hit the room like a bomb. And for the first time in his life, Thane’s perfect mask completely shattered.

###chapter 2
Nobody bought it. Not for a second. Six times they shoved the divorce papers in Elara’s face, and six times the Managing Director threw them back. She’d sat there and taken it while her old nanny’s kid strutted around her house like she paid the mortgage. The whole pack talked trash behind her back. They laughed. They felt sorry for her. In their eyes, she was just a pushover.

Then she spoke, and the room went dead silent. Like a knife hitting the floor. 

"No way," someone in the back muttered. "She’s bluffing. She’ll come crawling back. She always does." 

Another guy snorted. "Duh. Elara’s not dumping Chief Commander Thane. She loves her fancy title too much to walk."

Thane stood right in the middle of the room, looking like a million bucks in a custom cream suit. But for a split second, his smug face cracked. He figured she was playing games. I mean, the guy was the number-two big shot in the whole New York scene. Rich, powerful, dangerous. He could crush her with a phone call. Sure, the law protected Lunas, but laws have loopholes. Besides, this was embarrassing. He’d already talked so much trash about her before she even showed up.

He’d hyped this party up, sent out the invites weeks ago. Big-time Alphas blew off major meetings just to watch her beg. Thane was 100% sure she’d fold like a cheap tent. But this? This cold shoulder? It threw him off. Almost every heavy hitter in the city was in the room. Only a couple of guys missed it—like his best bud Orion from Grimroot, who couldn't make it.

"You're making a mistake," Thane finally said, keeping his voice cool and steady. He stared her down, sizing her up. "You know the rules. You divorce a Chief Commander, and you're blacklisted. No other Commander will touch you." 

The crowd of Alphas mumbled, nodding along. 

Thane puffed out his chest. "We have a pact, Elara. We don't do hand-me-downs. You won't even land a beta. You'll end up with some bottom-tier nobody."

He looked at her like she was trash. He meant it, too. But Elara didn't blink. She'd seen that look a thousand times. Even in a cheap, paper-thin hospital gown, she stood tall, shoulders back, chin up. Thane looked exactly like he did the night she fell for him—on that hill during the Moon Festival when she turned eighteen. Her heart had been pounding out of her chest when she yelled to everyone, "Thane is mine!"

Back then, the crowd had stared at him, waiting. He just shrugged it off. Later, he told everyone, "I'm with Briar. She's actually sweet, unlike Elara." Since Elara grew up as a beta's kid, everyone called her a spoiled princess. But Briar? She was a professional victim. Tears on cue, soft voice, the whole nine yards. She claimed Elara bullied her, and everyone bought it hook, line, and sinker—Thane, the pack, even Elara's own folks. Elara never argued. She figured the truth would come out eventually.

What a joke that was. 

"Hey, Thane," Elara said, her voice cutting right through the chatter. "I'm the Managing Director. You seriously think I don't know how a divorce works?" 

Her eyes were dead, totally blank. For once, Thane looked nervous. No crying, no begging. Just a creepy, quiet vibe that freaked him out.

"You've got some nerve," he spat. "You trapped me. You got my parents to force this marriage, and now you're playing the victim?" 

"Just take the damn papers," Elara interrupted, shoving the signed documents right under his nose.

Thane froze, staring at the pages. Then Briar slid in next to him, wearing a sparkly gold dress that made her blonde hair look like a shampoo commercial. She had this tiny, smug smirk. 

"Oh, Elara," Briar purred, sounding totally fake-nice. "Thane only asked for my help because you were out cold. Now that you're awake, we can just call off the party. No need to get a divorce, right?"

Elara forced a smile, but her eyes stayed ice-cold. She wanted to scream, wanted to call out the bullshit right then and there. But with all these eyes on her, she kept her mouth shut. She scanned the room. "Where's Asher?" Her chest tightened. He wasn't there.

"School," Thane muttered, sounding a bit jumpy. 

"He's the only thing I'm taking with me," Elara said. 

"No way!" Thane and Briar yelled together.

Elara raised an eyebrow, totally unfazed. She didn't need a fancy title to look like a boss. Even in a hospital gown, she owned the room. "You honestly thought I'd leave my kid with you?" 

Thane shot a look at Briar, then grabbed Elara's arm and dragged her to the side. "Stop embarrassing me," he hissed. "I'll explain later. Just go." 

She didn't say a word. She just turned on her heel and left.

The school was close, but that thirty-minute walk felt like a marathon. Her chest ached with every step. She was still weak, but she kept moving. When Asher saw her, his face fell. "Why are you here?" he snapped.

It hurt like hell, but she forced a smile and reached for his arm. "Hey, buddy. Sorry I was gone so long. Let's go home, okay?" 

"No way," Asher yelled, ripping his arm back. "I hate you!"

The words hit her like a punch. She thought he'd be happy to see her. Not this. Not from her own kid. 

"Asher," she said, trying to keep her voice from shaking. "I'm your mom. We're leaving this place. You're coming with me." 

She reached out again, but he jumped back like she was radioactive. "No!" he screamed. "You're not my mom! Get away from me!"

People started staring. Elara forced a fake smile, keeping her voice down. "Hey, look, you're mad, but don't say that." 

Before she could grab him, a teacher walked out. "Oh, Managing Director?" the guy gasped. "You're awake? Briar said you were a goner." 

Elara ignored him, keeping her eyes on her kid. "I'm taking Asher."

The teacher stepped in her way. "Uh, sorry, ma'am. Thane said only Briar has custody of the kid now." 

Elara froze. 

"Actually," the teacher mumbled, looking uncomfortable, "he said Briar is his real mom."

Something in her brain just broke. "Are you freaking crazy?" she snapped. 

The teacher shook his head. "I thought so too. Until I saw the DNA test." He handed her a piece of paper. 

Her eyes went blurry. Her legs turned to jelly. "No way..." she whispered, her voice cracking. "This is fake. Asher is my..." 

The ground rushed up to meet her.

###chapter 3
"Mom! Thank god you're here," a kid whimpered, sounding totally freaked. "That psycho tried to kidnap me."

"Hey, it's okay, buddy," a woman's voice cut in, smooth but dead serious. "Nobody's touching you. Your dad's got this."

Elara heard them before she could even blink. The words buzzed in her skull, fuzzy and annoying, like a bad hangover. 

She forced her eyes open. The ceiling of the pack house stared back—rough wooden beams, blurry as hell, like she was looking up from the bottom of a pool. 

She had zero clue how she ended up on this bed. The last thing she remembered? Her legs turning to jelly and that damn DNA report slipping from her shaking hands, fluttering down to the floor.

Wait, this was crazy. Her chest throbbed. She knew she was pregnant. It happened right after that wild, rough night Thane claimed her—the night that locked her into the marriage she’d secretly craved. 

She’d dragged herself through nine brutal months of puke, bone-deep fatigue, and pure agony. She went into labor. She screamed, she bled, she heard a baby cry. Then she blacked out. She had the kid. So what the hell was this?

Thane’s face came into focus. His eyes were pure ice, glaring down at her with raw hate. "You got a death wish?" he spat. "Who the hell do you think you are, trying to run off with my kid?"

Elara kept her face blank. Lysander grabbed her arm, pulling her up. Her body was one giant bruise, but she tuned it out, her brain firing on all cylinders. Over by the wall, Briar was just standing there, wearing this smug, nasty little grin. She wasn't even trying to hide how thrilled she was.

"Thane," Elara said, keeping her voice dead level while her insides screamed. "I gave birth to a boy. If Asher isn't mine, then where is my actual son?"

Thane let out a nasty laugh, his eyes turning pitch black. "Are you stupid?" he sneered. "You drugged me to get into my bed. You seriously thought I'd let you keep my kid after that?"

He dropped the next words like a bomb, slow and brutal. "Briar popped that same night. I made sure your kid disappeared."

Something snapped in Elara's head. She lost it. Screaming like a wild animal, she threw herself at him, fingers clawing for his throat, her fangs sliding out, ready to rip him open.

Thane didn't even sweat. He caught her, flipped her, and slammed her hard onto the floorboards. The impact knocked the wind right out of her, pain shooting straight to her bones.

"You're tough," Thane said, standing over her like a giant. "But I'm the Chief Commander. Nobody beats me."

Elara dragged herself up, her arms shaking, her brain totally numb. "No," she croaked. "Where's my boy?"

"You mean your girl," Thane shot back. "She never even got a breath of air. I burned her and mixed her ashes into the concrete of this very house."

The walls spun. Her knees gave out again, her eyes going blurry. It was all a lie. She'd spent years raising a kid that wasn't hers. She'd given up everything for Asher—even the rare cure for his genetic disease. She'd handed it over to save the kid of the monsters who killed her own baby.

It hit her like a truck. If she'd just signed those divorce papers sooner, she would've gone to her grave never knowing. Thane would've kept this sick secret forever.

"I didn't trap you," she whispered, her voice finally cracking. She never begged or made excuses, but she had to say it. "You took what you wanted from me that night. You forced it."

"Cut the crap," Thane barked. "We have the receipts. You paid off the bartender to drug my glass. If you hadn't, Briar would be running this place, not you. You messed with the wrong guy."

Elara went white. Why did she even bother? Thane had already made up his mind, and nothing she said mattered. Losing the guy you loved was bad enough. Finding out he murdered your baby? That was a whole different level of hell.

"Fine, believe whatever you want," she choked out, tears finally spilling over. "But she was your kid too. How could you be such a monster?"

Thane didn't even blink. "Exactly," he said, cold as ice. "She had my blood, which is why she had to go. Why do you think I never laid a finger on you again? You're pathetic, Elara."

She’d put up with this fake, loveless marriage for years, trying her best every single day to be the perfect wife and leader. She knocked back his divorce papers six times. Why? Because of the kid. She didn't want him growing up in a broken home.

But now? It was all a sick joke. Her heart was in a million pieces, and she didn't even know where to start picking them up.

Briar piped up, her voice dripping with fake sweetness. "Look, Elara, it's fine. I'm not mad. You can keep playing mommy to Asher. You've done a great job keeping him alive with that nasty disease of his."

The bitch was gloating. The subtext was loud and clear: *I killed your kid, and you're still keeping mine alive. Plus, I've got your cure.*

But Briar didn't know the catch. Nobody did. That medicine wasn't a permanent fix. It was a leash. Sure, Asher could run around and play as long as he took it. But miss just one dose? The sickness would hit him like a freight train.

That's why she'd tried to grab him. But now? Screw it. She didn't care anymore. A weird, icy calm settled over her, pumped up by pure adrenaline. She looked Thane dead in the eye.

"You killed my baby," she said, her voice barely a whisper but sharp as a knife. "And I saved yours. Let the spirits sort this out."

She turned on her heel and walked right past him, her boots heavy on the floor, just wanting to get out of this suffocating hellhole.

She almost made it to the door. Then she slammed right into a wall of solid muscle. The guy didn't budge an inch, radiating pure, terrifying power. She looked up. A pair of killer, pitch-black eyes stared down at her. Elara froze.

###chapter 4
Caspian wasn't just some big shot running the Grimroot Consortium. The guy was a god. His name alone made Wall Street sweat. He was the baddest boss to ever come out of the East Coast, loaded enough to buy entire countries, and hot enough to make people stop and stare. One word from him, and billion-dollar companies folded. One look, and tough-guy Alphas backed down. Power just stuck to him.

But there was a catch. Everyone knew Caspian couldn't stand women. Rumor had it he was either gay or literally allergic to them. That’s why people whispered. The packs couldn't figure out why the country’s most eligible bachelor didn't have a mate, or why Grimroot still didn't have a first lady. See, when Caspian wanted something, he took it. No hesitation. So why was his bed empty?

Elara’s boot caught on a jagged stone. Her bum leg gave out, and she started to go down. She would’ve hit the dirt hard, but a heavy hand locked onto her arm and yanked her back up. Rough, but steady.

"Watch your step," Caspian muttered. Same old voice—cold, sharp, like a switchblade.

Elara didn't look at him for long. "Yeah. Thanks for the save," she spat, her voice dripping with sweet poison.

Then she ripped her arm away. She bolted down the hall, gone like a ghost before he could even blink. Caspian stared after her way longer than he should have, his jaw tight as her perfume faded from the air.

Elara didn't slow down. She ran straight to the pack hospital. If there were any answers left, they’d be in there. The place was dead quiet. Under the buzzing fluorescent lights, she tore through rooms, ripping open cabinets and grabbing files with shaking hands. Medical charts, birth records, death certificates—anything to prove how her baby girl had supposedly died.

Her chest was hammering, but she knew she was on her own. Then she spotted Lysander hovering by the door. "Hey, Lysander," she said quietly. "Aren't you scared your big boss will catch you?"

Lysander went stiff. He opened his mouth, choked on his words, and swallowed hard. "Ma'am... what are you looking for?"

Elara spun around. Ever since she’d walked into this clinic, people had treated her like the plague. Nurses looked away. Researchers ducked into offices. Doctors who used to kiss her feet now acted like she was invisible. She was the one who ran their lab, cured their sick, and even made the drug that fixed her own paralysis. Now? She was trash. But she didn't give a damn. If she found one lead on her baby, she was out of here.

"Lysander," she said, keeping her voice dangerously soft. "Talk to me. What happened to my daughter? How did she die?"

Lysander’s shoulders slumped. He stared at his shoes, looking miserable. "They told me to kill her, ma'am."

Elara froze. The papers slipped right through her fingers and hit the floor.

"But I couldn't do it," he choked out.

Elara’s head snapped up. A sudden, painful jolt of hope hit her chest. "So she’s alive?" she whispered. "Oh my god, she’s alive, right? Where is she? Tell me!"

Lysander shook his head, looking like he wanted to cry. "I don't know. That night, I saw some woman crossing the border. I panicked and dumped the kid on her before the guards caught me. I didn't even get her name." He balled his fists. "I killed a wild animal instead, burned it, and handed the ashes to Thane as proof."

Elara finally let out the breath she’d been holding. Relief hit her like a truck. Her knees shook, but her heart was racing with real hope. Her baby was alive.

"What did the woman look like? Describe her," she demanded.

Lysander shook his head again. "It was pitch black. I couldn't see a thing, I'm sorry. Look, I hated you back then. I wanted to do what I was told. But the baby started crying..." His voice cracked. "I just couldn't."

A single tear rolled down Elara’s cheek, but she was smiling. "Thank you," she whispered, her voice shaking. "Man, if I’d known this, I would’ve signed those divorce papers years ago." She wouldn't have waited for him to screw her over seven times.

She turned back to the shelves, grabbing folders left and right. Lysander frowned. "What are you doing?"

"They tried to murder my baby," she said, her voice turning to ice. "Why the hell should they keep my life's work?"

She marched over to the medicine cabinet, popping open vial after vial and dumping the priceless liquids right down the sink. Years of research, miracle cures—gone.

"Let Briar figure it out herself," Elara muttered. "If she even has a brain."

The last glass vial clinked against the drain. She’d wanted to leave quietly, but they’d ripped her heart out. As of right now, she was done with the Centenary Syndicate.

By the time she got back to the pack house, it was dark. Laughter drifted from Thane’s office—loud, mocking, irritating. Elara ignored it.

She went straight to her room, took a fast shower to wash the pack’s stink off her skin, and threw on some clean clothes. The only thing she packed was a stack of her own research papers—seven years of her life in a folder.

She was almost out the door when a voice stopped her. "So, you finally figured out you don't belong here, huh?" It was Briar.

Elara turned around slowly, a smirk tugging at her lips. "Well, look who’s finally showing her real face."

Briar stood there, looking smug, eyeing the room like she already owned it. "You actually thought being some beta's kid made you special?" she sneered. "Wrong. I'm the boss now. I got your man, I got your kid killed, and you spent years raising mine."

Elara smiled, but her eyes were dead. "It's your show now," she said softly. "Have fun with it."

Briar’s face fell. This wasn't the reaction she wanted. She wanted Elara begging on her knees, broken. If Elara wouldn't do it herself, Briar would make her.

Briar looked around, spotted a knife in the fruit basket, and grabbed it. She sliced it hard across her own wrist, dropped the blade, and let out a bloody-murder scream.

"Help!" Briar shrieked. "Thane! She's trying to kill me!"

Heavy footsteps pounded up the stairs. Thane burst in first, with Caspian right behind him. Elara hadn't realized Caspian was still around.

Thane scooped Briar up like she was made of glass, glaring at Elara with pure hatred. "You... how could you do this?"

Elara’s lips curved into a slow, nasty grin. "You really believe every single thing she says, don't you?" she said easily. "Fine."

She stepped forward, snatched the knife off the floor, and drove it straight into Briar’s other wrist.

"There," Elara said, her eyes burning cold. "Now I actually did it. What are you gonna do about it?"

Both Alphas froze. But it was the look in Elara’s eyes—zero regrets, zero fear—that absolutely terrified Briar. The shock knocked the tears right out of her.

For the first time, Briar realized something. Elara was completely out of their control. And nobody, not even Thane, could touch her now.

###chapter 5
Briar’s legs gave out. Thane caught her mid-drop, scooped her up, and let out a guttural roar. The copper stink of fresh blood hit his nose hard. It triggered his inner beast. He spun on his heel, aiming for the medical wing, but Briar’s shaking fingers yanked his shirt collar.

"Rav... wait," she wheezed. "She’s running."

Thane froze. He blinked, tracking Briar’s gaze.

Red pooled from Briar’s wrists, soaking his sleeves. But Briar didn't care about the cuts. She stared straight at Elara. Elara stood a few feet away, back straight, a tiny duffel bag sitting by her boots.

"Running?" Thane’s voice cracked. No way. That bag couldn't hold her life. "Where the hell is she going?"

It was past midnight. The mansion was dead quiet. Long, creepy shadows stretched across the marble floor. That stupid little bag made his stomach twist with pure rage.

Briar wasn't about to let Elara just walk. No freaking way. Elara had played queen for too long. Just once, Briar wanted to watch her hit rock bottom.

"It’s just a scratch," Briar lied quickly, keeping her voice steady but tight. "It'll heal. Eventually." She gulped, ramping up the drama. "But her? She tried to bolt. I tried to stop her, and she freaking stabbed me."

The lie hung in the air. Elara tilted her head. A smirk played on her lips.

"Still a liar, I see," Elara said. Her voice was cool. Way too cool. But those icy blue eyes flashed with a promise that made Briar shrink back.

"Aren't you scared of what I'll do next?" Elara whispered.

Briar flinched. Thane snapped.

"Lysander!" he bellowed, shaking the walls.

Heavy boots pounded the stairs. Lysander appeared, stiff and ready for a fight. "Chief Commander."

Thane glared at Elara like she was trash, then locked eyes with Lysander. "Throw her in the dungeon," he barked, pointing a finger. "Keep her there till I figure out how to ruin her."

Nobody breathed. But Lysander didn't budge. "Can't do that, sir."

"Excuse me?" Thane snarled, pivoting. His fuse was gone. "I said, lock her up."

The dungeon was old-school. They used to throw rogue wolves and traitors in there back when things were bloody. Now? Nobody used it. It had been gathering dust for ten years.

"Sorry, Chief," Lysander said, his voice flat but stubborn. "I'm not doing it."

A collective gasp sucked the air out of the room. Elara’s eyes went wide. Caspian’s did too.

"She’s still my boss," Lysander added.

Briar bit her lip, trying not to scream. What did Elara have on this guy? Why the hell did he respect her so much?

Thane let out a nasty laugh. "We're getting a divorce," he spat. "She signed the papers. She’s not your Managing Director anymore."

Lysander didn't blink. "Then do it yourself, Chief. The paperwork isn't processed yet. Technically, she’s still my boss. Only you have the legal right to lay a hand on her."

The logic was airtight. Thane hated it. Gritting his teeth, he set Briar down on a chair. He stood up, squared his shoulders, and stalked toward Elara like a predator.

Elara kept her chin up. Zero fear. "Touch me," she dared, "and I’m calling the Council. You know what they'll do to you."

Thane sneered. "The Council needs proof. Witnesses. You’ve got zero."

God, he hated her. He hated how she stood between him and Briar. He hated that she was a walking reminder of a bond he wanted dead and buried.

Well, at least she signed the papers. Soon, she’d be nobody.

"I'm her witness."

Lysander’s voice sliced through the room. Thane froze, jaw dropping.

"Do you have any idea what you're saying right now?" Thane growled, his eyes turning murderous.

Lysander stared right back. "Yeah, Chief. I do." He reached into his jacket, pulled out a white envelope, and slapped it into Thane’s hand. "Which is why I'm quitting. Consider this my resignation as Deputy."

The world spun. Even Caspian, who’d been playing spectator, couldn't stay quiet. "Are you seriously throwing your pack away," he gasped, "for a woman like her?"

He couldn't even find the words to insult Elara properly. Lysander turned to him, totally calm. "Caspian," he said, "watch your mouth."

Briar’s eyes darted back and forth. Panic set in. She saw Caspian’s gaze soften as he looked at Elara. She couldn't let that happen.

"She’s never going to leave Thane!" Briar blurted. "She used to brag about it constantly. Ask anyone in the pack, or the other Lunas! If she crawls back to him, Lysander, you’re going to look like a total clown."

Lysander gave a cold, faint smile. "I'm not quitting because of Elara."

"Then why?" Thane and Caspian demanded together.

Lysander swallowed. "It's personal."

Elara let out a dry laugh. "Honestly? I hope you two live happily ever after," she said, deadpan. "Now that I think about it, you two idiots deserve each other."

"Seriously, sweetie, you nailed it this time," Eleanor said, her voice thick with pure, unfiltered pride. "You got a real one."

"God, if we had any clue Thane was such a psycho, we would've forced the issue with your memory. We would've fought dirty. But whatever, that's over." She let out a shaky, emotional laugh. "You have Caspian now. Game over. He changes the whole playing field."

The line went dead quiet. Sera was clearly putting the puzzle pieces together, fast.

Her parents were hours away. You don't just make that drive on a whim. And Caspian was supposed to grab her soon for the pack trip. So when the hell did he find the time to—

"Wait, is Caspian with you guys?" Sera asked, her voice cracking with a mix of shock and this sudden, sweet warmth.

"Nope, just missed him," Eleanor beamed. "He literally flew in on a chopper, said he had to rush back to get you to some shaman tonight. Oh my god, Sera." She softened her voice, getting all mushy.

"I saw how he looked when he talked about you. Seriously, no wonder he let you slap him—twice, was it?—when he was acting like an arrogant prick. A guy who's over you doesn't look at you like that. He never stopped loving you, sweetie. Not for a single second."

Those words punched Sera right in the gut, sending her emotions into a tailspin.

She could still feel those two slaps. The first was pure panic and rage, just trying to survive. The second was basically the same. And Caspian just stood there and took it. No grabbing, no screaming, none of the toxic garbage other guys would've pulled.

He let her get away with it. Nobody else on the planet could've done that to him.

Right there, she made a quiet vow to herself. Never again. Not because she was scared, but because he didn't deserve it. The guessing game was over. He loved her, period. And he wasn't the type to lash out or play mind games. She didn't have to test him anymore.

"Thanks, guys," she choked out, her voice thick with tears. "Mom, Dad... thank you. Seriously. You're coming, right?"

Arthur snorted, laughing. "Try stopping us. We're the parents of the bride, kiddo. We're showing up early, crashing the place, the whole nine yards." He was grinning ear to ear, and he didn't care who knew it.

Eleanor nodded vigorously, forgetting Sera couldn't see her. "Yeah, we're staying over. You better have a guest room prepped."

"I'd love that so much," Sera whispered, her voice cracking.

The line went dead. Arthur stood there, hand resting near his phone, just riding the wave of relief. No drama. Just a rare, genuinely good moment.

Sera flipped her phone face-down on the table. She sat there, letting the silence settle around her.

She never saw that call coming. Honestly, she hadn't expected any of Caspian's behind-the-scenes moves today—quietly checking in on everyone she cared about before she even knew what he was up to.

No bragging, no looking for a pat on the back. He just handled it. Quiet, solid, and protective.

She was still processing all of this when Lysander strolled into the room, holding a thick, glossy magazine open to a massive spread of wedding dresses.

"Hey, Sera," he said, shoving it toward her. "Pick a dress before we hit the road. I want to get the designer started tonight so they can work on it while we're away." He shrugged like it was no big deal. "Oh, and I already grabbed your measurements."

Sera stared at the glossy pages, her brain short-circuiting. The dress. She'd completely blanked on it. With all the chaos, a wedding gown was the last thing on her mind. But looking at it now, she didn't feel like grabbing it.

Her first wedding had been a total joke compared to this.

Thane didn't give a shit. He just showed up, did the bare minimum, and checked out. She'd picked out every single detail herself—the cut, the color, everything—because why ask a guy who wasn't even looking? She dressed for herself because nobody else cared.

But Caspian actually cared.

He noticed the little things, the way only someone who truly loved you would. Sera wanted to wear a dress that would make his jaw drop.

"Hey, do you know what kind of style he likes?" she asked, looking up at Lysander. "He's done so much for me. I want this wedding to be about him, too, not just me picking random stuff."

Lysander paused, thinking. Then his face lit up and he snapped the magazine shut. "Actually, scratch that. I'll just ask him. He styled that whole Dominic look himself, so the guy's got taste." He nodded. "I'll corner him tonight, get his vision, and we'll build the dress around that."

The knot in Sera's chest finally unraveled. "Perfect. Thank you."

The rest of the afternoon was a total blur. She was a ball of nerves and excitement, her heart racing at the thought of finally seeing her little girl back home.

And then there was the shaman. She tried not to overthink it. Would it work? Would she wake up tomorrow as a completely different person? She forced the thoughts down, focused on packing, her chest tight.

When she finally walked out to the driveway, the cool night air hit her, and she stopped dead in her tracks.

Something felt seriously wrong.

She stood there, trying to figure out the vibe. It wasn't a threat, exactly. Just this weird, nagging pull. Like she had unfinished business she needed to wrap up before she could leave in peace.

She looked over at Lysander, who was waiting by the door. "Hey, can we make a quick detour to the Stone mansion first?" She locked eyes with him. "I need to see Uncle Felix and Aunt Lyra."

His eyes flickered, but he didn't ask questions or push back. "Yeah," he said after a second. "Sure. Let's do it."

Neither of them said it out loud, but Lysander needed this stop just as much. His parents deserved to hear it directly from him, face-to-face, that he was moving out. He owed them that much respect.

He popped the passenger door open, and Sera slid inside. They drove off in silence.

But what neither of them realized was that someone had already beaten them to the house.

Caspian grew up in places like this. They never intimidated him. But walking up those steps tonight? Totally different vibe. He wasn't here to play the big bad alpha. He was here to pay a debt.
